scalars.scalar_value: Experience providing psychological services to adult populations

items.item_text: PhD or PsyD in Clinical Psychology from an APA-accredited program
Experience providing psychological services to adult populations
Experience training and supervising predoctoral and/or postdoctoral psychology trainees
Experience working with patients with psychiatric conditions and co-occurring medical illnesses

The Department of Psychiatry is seeking to hire a part-time limited Psychologist II to join our Health Psychology and Trauma Clinic, a specialized program focused on addressing the psychological impact of medical illness, trauma, and complex psychiatry conditions. Working alongside an interdisciplinary team, ,you will provide high-quality inpatient and outpatient services for adults presenting with psychiatric and co-occurring medical disorders. Key responsibilities include:
Conduct comprehensive clinical interviews, psychological assessments, and evidence-based psychotherapy with inpatient and outpatient populations
Administer, score, and interpret psychological tests and provide feedback to patients and families
Develop clinical reports, treatment recommendations, and maintain timely clinical documentation and billing records
Provide supervision, training, and mentorship to psychology interns and postdoctoral fellows
Collaborate closely with psychologists and multidisciplinary teams within the clinic to support patient care and treatment planning
Adhere to professional, ethical, and regulatory standards while ensuring high-quality patient-centered care
Please note: this is a limited position that may convert to career
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Outlook, and Excel
Formal postdoctoral training in Health Psychology
Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills
Ability to work effectively with individuals from diverse backgrounds
Strong organizational skills and ability to maintain accurate clinical records
